entry.name: jweb~
entry.description: The jweb~ object uses the cross-platform Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) to host web pages within a Max UI object. Audio signals generated by the page are sent out the object's outlets.

attributes.name: latency
attributes.digest: Latency (ms)
attributes.description: Sets the output latency in milliseconds. Setting the latency to 0 will set the minimum possible latency (around 23ms at 44.1kHz sampling rate; around 21ms at 48kHz). The minimum latency may result in occasionaly drop-outs or distortion. The maximum latency is three times the minimum.

attributes.name: rendermode
attributes.digest: Page rendering style
attributes.description: When theattribute is set to ‘offscreen’,will first render to an offscreen buffer, then draw to the patcher window. This mode is slower, but useful if you need UI elements to appear in front of theobject. When set to ‘onscreen’,will render faster, but render directly in the patcher (without using an offscreen buffer), drawing over any other UI elements. When set to 'onscreen with transparent background', the background of theobject will be rendered transparently.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.description: Use the mouse (and keyboard) to interact with the page displayed byin a locked patcher.

messages.name: anything
messages.description: You can send any message to the JavaScript of the contained website. In order to be able to receive messages make sure to setup the JavaScript as described in theguide.

messages.name: back
messages.description: Themessage reloads the previous page of data, functioning like the 'Back' button in a conventional web browser.

messages.name: executejavascript
messages.description: Usingyou can inject and run a JavaScript code snippet in the currently displayed web page. The provided code will be inserted and executed in a new script tag.

messages.name: forward
messages.digest: Move forward in visited page history
messages.description: When a sequence of multiple pages has been loaded, and the object has received themessage, the wordwill advance to the following page in the object's page history.functions like the 'Forward' button in a conventional web browser.

messages.name: gotohistory
messages.digest: Navigate to a page in the browser history
messages.description: If theattribute has been set to a named dictionary,followed by an index will navigate to the page with that index in the dictionary. The most recently visited page is stored at index 0.

messages.name: mute
messages.description: will mute the signal output of the page;will unmute

messages.name: read
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies a URL or a file pathname, will read the webpage or file and attempt to render its contents. Upon successful load of a page, two messages are sent from the object's outlet:, followed the final URL which was loaded based on the provided argument; and, followed by the title of the loaded page as a symbol.

messages.name: readfile
messages.description: The word, followed by a symbol that specifies a file pathname, will read the file and attempt to render its contents. The wordwith no argument opens a file dialog to choose a file. Upon successful load of a page, two messages are sent from the object's outlet:, followed the final URL which was loaded based on the provided argument; and, followed by the title of the loaded page as a symbol.

messages.name: reload
messages.description: Themessage causes the browser to refresh the current page, functioning like the 'Reload' button in a conventional web browser. The wordfollowed by a non-zero argument will ignore the locally cached file.
